prompt_c2:
You are a streetscape inventory annotator. Look ONLY at the uploaded streetscape image.
Return JSON ONLY. No markdown, no commentary, no reasoning.
 Task: record what is visible in the scene. Do not score, do not give design advice.
 Schema:
{
"road_type": "highway|arterial|neighborhood_street|alley|plaza|unclear",
"elements": {
"sidewalk": "true|false|unclear",
"bike_lane": "true|false|unclear",
"seating": "true|false|unclear",
"shade_trees": "none|few|many|unclear",
"curb_ramp": "true|false|unclear",
"tactile_paving": "true|false|unclear",
"pedestrian_crossing": "true|false|unclear",
"street_lighting": "true|false|unclear",
"greenery": "none|low|medium|high|unclear",
"vehicle_traffic": "none|light|heavy|unclear",
"bus_stop": "true|false|unclear"
},
"issues": ["no_seating", "little_shade", "no_bike_lane", "poor_accessibility", "narrow_sidewalk", "no_crossing", "high_traffic_exposure"],
"brief": "One or two English sentences describing the visible street scene."
}
 Rules:
- If an element is not clearly visible, use "unclear". Do not guess.
- "issues" may only list problems that are visible. Use [] if none.
- "brief" must mention concrete objects (sidewalk, trees, lanes, benches, ramps, etc.).

When setting street trees, full consideration shall be given to their relative relationship with traffic signs, information boards, etc. The spacing between trees in front of traffic signs and information boards may be increased to around 18 m. Where obstruction has already formed in the existing condition, trees shall be pruned according to actual conditions, or the position, style, and height of the signs shall be adjusted. 3.3 Median strips 3.3.1 Design 1. Definition The green partition between carriageways; the one located between the upstream and downstream motor vehicle lanes is the central median; the one located between motor vehicle lanes and non-motorized lanes or between motor vehicle lanes in the same direction is the side median. 2. Layout forms A. Central median a. The central median of urban arterial roads with a design speed higher than 60 km/h shall be densely planted with evergreen plants to avoid glare interference from oncoming traffic at night. 70 b. Within the range of 0.6 m to 1.5 m above the surface of the adjacent motor vehicle roadway, the plants configured shall have dense foliage throughout the year, and their spacing shall not be greater than 5 times the canopy spread. c. The width of the central median shall be 1.5 m or more, and a formal arrangement structure shall be adopted; simple repetition is preferable to create rhythm. At intersections and important nodes, plants shall mainly be low shrubs; planting trees is strictly prohibited to avoid tree trunks causing glare and traffic accidents. Figure 3.3-1 Schematic diagram of central median B. Side median a. Where the width of the side green belt between carriageways is greater than or equal to 1.5 m, trees shall be the main planting type, and trees, shrubs, and groundcover plants should be combined. The canopies of trees on both sides should not overlap above the motor vehicle lanes. b. Where the width of the side green belt between carriageways is less than 1.5 m, shrubs shall be the main planting type, and shrubs and groundcover plants should be combined. 71 Figure 3.3-2 Schematic diagram of central median C. Characteristic island heads a. Quality enhancement of island-head flower borders and landscape stones shall be carried out on the premise of not affecting driving sight distance, not obstructing traffic signs, signal monitoring facilities, or lighting effects. b. It is encouraged to set up Suzhou-specific rockery stones and pruned topiary forms, creating a regional garden-style landscape with varied stone forms, distinct layers of vegetation, and brightly colored flowers. c. When the width of the side median is less than 2 m, the length of characteristic greening at the island head should be controlled at 5–10 m. A

Quality improvement of non-motorized vehicle lane paving In riverside greenways and other leisure spaces, or at locations with a significantly high incidence of traffic accidents involving motor vehicles and non-motorized vehicles, non-motorized vehicle lanes may use colored paving. Isolation facilities may be appropriately arranged to improve the cycling experience for non-motorized vehicles. Figure 1.4-1 Schematic diagram of non-motorized vehicle lane paving 2. Paving design shall implement the concepts of safety, health, comfort, and people-oriented design. Figure 1.4-2 Example of paving for traffic-function roads B. Living-service roads The activity groups on living-service roads include residents and workers around the road, as well as people from other areas who come for shopping and strolling. Roundabouts** A. Conventional roundabouts should not be used at urban arterial road intersections. For roads approaching an intersection on a grade, when the longitudinal gradient is ≥3%, a roundabout at-grade intersection should not be adopted. Roundabout at-grade intersections shall not be used on expressways or on major arterials with heavy traffic volumes. B. For the reconstruction of existing large roundabouts or where special needs exist, the requirements may be relaxed. **2.2.6 Sight Distance Requirements** Landscaping and greenery within the sight triangle of at-grade intersections shall remain visually open and unobstructed. Obstacles that obstruct the driver’s line of sight within the sight triangle of an at-grade intersection shall be removed. Greenery higher than 1.2 m that obstructs the driver’s line of sight is not permitted. **2.3 Grade-separated Intersections** When expressways intersect with urban roads of all classes, grade-separated intersections must be adopted; when expressways intersect with expressways, grade-separated intersections must be adopted; when expressways intersect with arterial roads, grade-separated intersections shall be adopted. The conditions for setting up grade-separated crossings between roads and railways are as follows: A. Grade-separated intersections must be provided where expressways cross railways. B. Grade-separated intersections shall be provided where arterial roads, secondary arterial roads, and branch roads cross railways and where traffic volume at the crossing is high or railway shunting operations are frequent and the cumulative closure time of the crossing is long. C. Grade-separated intersections shall be provided where arterial roads and secondary arterial roads cross railways and where, during peak road traffic periods, long single-closure periods occur frequently. D. Grade-separated intersections shall be provided where roads used by trams or trolleybuses cross railways. 35 **2.4 Roads** **2.4.1 New Construction Projects** Urban road traffic design shall follow the following principles: 1. People-oriented: importance shall be attached to the functional requirements of urban roads in shaping the environment and enhancing road vitality, and importance shall be attached to road landscape design with natural and humanistic features to create a pleasant road traffic environment. 2. System coordination: the designed road shall be incorporated into the overall urban road network, with full consideration of land-use functions and traffic characteristics within the road influence area, so as to achieve integration and coordination between land use functions and the transport system. 3. As a city streetscape evaluation expert, please analyze the uploaded streetscape image based on the specified persona perspective and evaluation indicators, and return a JSON result.
 Persona Selection
Road User Type
- All Road Users
- Pedestrians
- Cyclists
- Drivers
Socially Vulnerable Groups
- All Social Groups
- Persons with Disabilities
- Adolescents (<18)
- Older Adults (≥60)
Current Selection:
All Road Users; All Social Groups
 Indicator Selection
Justice
- Equity
- Fairness
- Accessibility
Safety
Livability
Sustainability
Aesthetics
Comfort
- Thermal Comfort
- Physical Comfort
- Psychological Comfort
Walkability
Bikeability
Selected Indicators:
Justice; Safety; Livability; Sustainability; Aesthetics; Comfort; Walkability
 1. Evaluation Dimensions
Justice: Analyze whether the environment fairly distributes spatial resources, including Equity (rationality of asset distribution), Fairness (non-discriminatory rules), and Accessibility (barrier-free physical design).
Comfort: Analyze physical perception at a micro-scale, including Thermal Comfort (shade/vegetation), Physical Comfort (paving/seating), and Psychological Comfort (noise/crowding).
Core Indicators: Safety, Livability, Sustainability, Aesthetics, Walkability, and Bikeability.
 2. Persona Perspective Requirements:
The analysis must strictly adhere to the persona's characteristics. For example:
Persons with Disabilities: Focus on curb ramps, continuity of tactile paving (blind tracks), and physical obstacles.
Elderly: Focus on resting facilities, slope gradients, and summer shade.
Teenagers: Focus on traffic calming measures and social surveillance (Eyes on the street).
 3. How to use the image vs retrieved knowledge:
- The IMAGE is the primary evidence. Score only what is visible or reasonably inferable from the photo.
- Section 6 provides retrieved guidelines and research. Use them to interpret the image (what the scene should provide for this persona/indicators), not to invent objects that are not in the photo.
- If retrieved text conflicts with the image, trust the image and say so in the explanation.
- Explanations must cite specific visible objects (benches, ramps, tree shade, lane markings, etc.). When a guideline is used, briefly connect it to those objects.

Definition The green partition between carriageways; the one located between the upstream and downstream motor vehicle lanes is the central median; the one located between motor vehicle lanes and non-motorized lanes or between motor vehicle lanes in the same direction is the side median. 2. Layout forms A. Central median a. The central median of urban arterial roads with a design speed higher than 60 km/h shall be densely planted with evergreen plants to avoid glare interference from oncoming traffic at night. 70 b. The width of the central median shall be 1.5 m or more, and a formal arrangement structure shall be adopted; simple repetition is preferable to create rhythm. All manhole covers shall be flush with the sidewalk elevation and in good condition, and the strength of manhole covers must meet sidewalk traffic requirements. 3. Roundabouts** A. Conventional roundabouts should not be used at urban arterial road intersections. For roads approaching an intersection on a grade, when the longitudinal gradient is ≥3%, a roundabout at-grade intersection should not be adopted. Roundabout at-grade intersections shall not be used on expressways or on major arterials with heavy traffic volumes. B. The number of motor-vehicle lanes in the roundabout should preferably be arranged as 2 to 3 lanes. For the reconstruction of existing large roundabouts or where special needs exist, the requirements may be relaxed. **2.2.6 Sight Distance Requirements** Landscaping and greenery within the sight triangle of at-grade intersections shall remain visually open and unobstructed. Obstacles that obstruct the driver’s line of sight within the sight triangle of an at-grade intersection shall be removed. Greenery higher than 1.2 m that obstructs the driver’s line of sight is not permitted. **2.3 Grade-separated Intersections** When expressways intersect with urban roads of all classes, grade-separated intersections must be adopted; when expressways intersect with expressways, grade-separated intersections must be adopted; when expressways intersect with arterial roads, grade-separated intersections shall be adopted. The conditions for setting up grade-separated crossings between roads and railways are as follows: A. Grade-separated intersections must be provided where expressways cross railways. B. Grade-separated intersections shall be provided where arterial roads, secondary arterial roads, and branch roads cross railways and where traffic volume at the crossing is high or railway shunting operations are frequent and the cumulative closure time of the crossing is long. C. Grade-separated intersections shall be provided where arterial roads and secondary arterial roads cross railways and where, during peak road traffic periods, long single-closure periods occur frequently. D. Grade-separated intersections shall be provided where roads used by trams or trolleybuses cross railways. 35 **2.4 Roads** **2.4.1 New Construction Projects** Urban road traffic design shall follow the following principles: 1. People-oriented: importance shall be attached to the functional requirements of urban roads in shaping the environment and enhancing road vitality, and importance shall be attached to road landscape design with natural and humanistic features to create a pleasant road traffic environment. 2. System coordination: the designed road shall be incorporated into the overall urban road network, with full consideration of land-use functions and traffic characteristics within the road influence area, so as to achieve integration and coordination between land use functions and the transport system. 3. Functional matching: due consideration shall be given to the various use functions and attributes of roads, and the functional spatial requirements of various transport modes in the higher-level plan shall be coordinated and implemented, while meeting the needs of public activity space. 4. Safety and order: traffic safety hazards shall be reduced through facility layout, engineering, and management measures, with particular emphasis on protecting vulnerable road users such as pedestrians and cyclists, and ensuring orderly traffic flow. 5.
